# Multivariate hybrid data case
Let's start with simulating a data with 4 variables (2 functions and 2 regular). 

```{r}
set.seed(123)
par(mfrow = c(2, 4), pin = c(1, 1), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2), pty = "s")

# Common left singular vector u (1 x 50)
n <- 150
u <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)
u <- u / sqrt(sum(u^2))

# Variable 1: v1 ~ N(0,1) with random near-zero entries
m1 <- 20
v1 <- rnorm(m1, sd = 0.8)
zero_indices_v1 <- sample(1:m1, 5)  # Select 5 indices
v1[zero_indices_v1] <- v1[zero_indices_v1] * 1e-2 + rnorm(5, sd = 0.01)
v1 <- v1 / sqrt(sum(v1^2))
matplot(v1, type = 'l', main = 'v1, Regular')

X1 <- outer(u, v1)
image(X1, main = 'X1, Regular')

# Variable 2: structured functional vector (similar to y1)
m2 <- 40
x2 <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = m2)
v2 <- sin(x2)
v2[1:20] <- rnorm(20, sd = 0.05)  # Replace first 20 values with near-zero noise
v2 <- v2 / sqrt(sum(v2^2))
matplot(v2, type = 'l', main = 'v2, Functional')

X2 <- outer(u, v2)
image(X2, main = 'X2, Functional')

# Variable 3: structured functional vector (similar to y2)
m3 <- 30
x3 <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = m3)
v3 <- cos(2 * x3)
#v3[21:30] <- rnorm(10, sd = 0.05)  # Replace end with near-zero noise
v3 <- v3 / sqrt(sum(v3^2))
matplot(v3, type = 'l', main = 'v3, Functional')

X3 <- outer(u, v3)
image(X3, main = 'X3, Functional')

# Variable 4: v4 ~ N(0,1) with some added noise
m4 <- 10
v4 <- rnorm(m4) + rnorm(m4, sd = 0.05)
v4 <- v4 / sqrt(sum(v4^2))
matplot(v4, type = 'l', main = 'v4, Regular')

X4 <- outer(u, v4)
image(X4, main = 'X4, Regular')

# Combine all into clean and noisy hybrid matrices
X_hybrid_clean <- cbind(outer(u, v1), outer(u, v2), outer(u, v3), outer(u, v4))
X_hybrid_noisy <- cbind(X1, X2, X3, X4)


# Plot 3D image
#par(mfrow = c(1, 4), pin = c(1, 1), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2))
#image(X_hybrid_clean, main = "True image")
#persp(X_hybrid_clean, theta = 40, main = "True persp")
#image(X_hybrid_noisy, main = "Noisy image")
#persp(X_hybrid_noisy, theta = 40, main = "Noisy persp")
```

Defining objects:
```{r}
fd_object2 <- fdClass(data = as.matrix(X2),
                     argval = NULL, 
                     Smoothing_parameter = NULL,  
                     Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0,39, length.out = 20)))

rd_object1 <- rdClass(data = as.matrix(X1),
                     Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0,19, length.out = 10)))

rd_object4 <- rdClass(data = as.matrix(X4),
                     Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0,9, length.out = 5)))

fd_object3 <- fdClass(data = as.matrix(X3),
                     argval = NULL, 
                     Smoothing_parameter = NULL,  
                     Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0,29, length.out = 15)))


hd_list <- list(rd_object1, fd_object2, fd_object3, rd_object4) 
object_list <- hdClass(hdlist = hd_list,
                       argval = NULL, 
                       Smoothing_parameter = NULL,
                       Sparsity_parameter = round(seq(0,50, length.out = 20)))

# Combine matrices side by side
hd <- object_list
n <- nrow(hd); K_fold <- 5; sparse_tuning_type <- "soft"
n_var <- attr(object_list, "n_var") # Number of variables (# of matrices in object_list)
ncol <- data.frame(attr(object_list, "ncol")) # Number of columns of each matrix

####### Smoothing Parameter ##########
# Generate all combinations alphas (one row per combination)
smooth_tuning_col <- expand.grid(attr(object_list, "Smoothing_parameter_col")) # A matrix
smooth_tuning_row <- attr(object_list, "Smoothing_parameter") # A vector

####### level of sparsity (for both functional and non-functional data) #######
sparsity_row_list <- attr(object_list, "Sparsity_parameter")
sparsity_col_list <- attr(object_list, "Sparsity_parameter_col")

X_temp <- hd

# No smoothness list:
S_alpha_v <- list()
for (i in 1:n_var) {
  S_alpha_v[[i]] <- diag(ncol[,i])
}

# Tuning across sparsity levels using 1-SE rule
CV_score_sparse_u <- CV_score_sparse_v <- GCV_score_smooth_u <- GCV_score_smooth_v <- Inf
CV_scores_result_u <- CV_scores_result_v <- list()
CV_results <- list()

gamma_v <- rep(0, n_var)
for (i in 1:n_var) {
  gamma_Xi <- sparsity_col_list[[i]]
  cv_means <- cv_ses <- fold_errors_vec <- numeric(length(gamma_Xi))

  for (j in seq_along(gamma_Xi)) {
    gamma_v[i] <- gamma_Xi[j]

    cv_result <- cv_sparse_col_SE(data = X_temp,
                                  n_var = n_var,
                                  ncol = ncol,
                                  S_alpha_v = S_alpha_v,
                                  S_alpha_u = diag(nrow(X_temp)),
                                  K_fold = K_fold,
                                  sparse_tuning_result_u = 0,
                                  sparse_tuning_result_v = gamma_v,
                                  sparse_tuning_type = sparse_tuning_type)

    cv_means[j] <- cv_result$CV_error
    cv_ses[j] <- cv_result$SE
    #fold_errors_vec <- cv_result$fold_errors
  }
  
  CV_results[[i]] <- data.frame(gamma_Xi, cv_means, cv_ses)
  
  # 1-SE rule
  j_min <- which.min(cv_means)
  threshold <- cv_means[j_min] + cv_ses[j_min]
  j_1se <- max(which(cv_means <= threshold))  # Most sparse within 1-SE

  # Store results
  CV_scores_result_v[[i]] <- list(errors = cv_means, SEs = cv_ses)
  sparse_tuning_selection_v <- gamma_Xi[j_1se]
  gamma_v[i] <- sparse_tuning_selection_v
}
gamma_v
plot(CV_results[[1]]$cv_means, type = 'l')

```

```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}
result <-power_algo(data = X_temp,
                    n_var = n_var,
                    ncol = ncol,
                    sparse_tuning_result_u = 0, # A fixed number
                    sparse_tuning_result_v = gamma_v, # A vector (length = p)
                    S_alpha_v = S_alpha_v, # A list (lenght = p)
                    S_alpha_u = diag(nrow(X_temp)), # A matrix
                    sparse_tuning_type= sparse_tuning_type)

par(mfrow = c(2,4), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
matplot(v1/norm_vec(v1),type = "l", pch = 16, main ="v1")
points(result[[1]][1:20]/norm_vec(result[[1]][1:20]), type = "p", pch = 16, main = 'v1', col = 'red')

matplot(v2/norm_vec(v2), type = 'l', main ="v2")
points(result[[1]][21:60]/norm_vec(result[[1]][21:60]), type = 'l', main = 'v2', col = 'red')

matplot(v3/norm_vec(v3), type = 'l', main ="v3")
points(result[[1]][61:90]/norm_vec(result[[1]][61:90]), type = 'l', main = 'v3', col = 'red')

matplot(v4/norm_vec(v4),type = "p", pch = 16, main ="v4")
points(result[[1]][91:100]/norm_vec(result[[1]][91:100]), type = 'l', main = 'v2', col = 'red')

matplot(result[[1]][1:20], type = "p", pch = 16, main = 'v1')
matplot(result[[1]][21:60], type = 'l', main = 'v2')
matplot(result[[1]][61:90], type = 'l', main = 'v3')
matplot(result[[1]][91:100], type = "p", pch = 16, main = 'v4')
```
